kidney size in SGA babies does not differ from that of AGA babies.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the kidney development is delayed in preterm S GA infants, especially in the asymmetrical ones, during the first year after birth, but it catches up later.
the SGA preterm infant is born with a smaller kidney and the kidney continues to grow at a slower rate compared to the AGA preterm infant.
the kidney length of preterm SGA babies is reduced compared with that of AGA preterm babies, but that this difference diminishes during the first year.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the kidney length is a useful tool in the assessment of kidney size in preterm SCA infants during the first year.
